newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB faces many unsettled years due to EMU - Meyer.
newsitem.headline: SNB faces many unsettled years due to EMU - Meyer.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) chairman Hans Meyer said in a newspaper interview that European Monetary Union (EMU) would likely create an unsettled environment for the Swiss central bank for several years.
Meyer was quoted as saying the period of uncertainty could last "not (just) for two or three years, but for five or 10."
The remarks were made during the International Monetary Fund meetings in Washington and published on Thursday in the Basler Zeitung daily newspaper.

Meyer was also quoted as saying that it was possible that EMU would begin with a small group of countries. He was also quoted as saying that inclusion of countries such as Italy and Spain from the start of EMU's phase three, set for January 1, 1999, would be difficult.
Italy's inclusion from the start may cause concern about the stability of the new currency. But its exclusion could give rise to concerns about political stability.
